lastCompletedStory.title: Flag the same form at plan time as self-contaminating-search and record the class in patterns.md

nextStoryContext: Pushed a fifth OracleLintRule, 'self-contaminating-search', onto RULES (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:640-ish, now 5 entries) that imports the pure predicate findStoreReachingSearch from src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts (US-002) rather than re-implementing path parsing -- this is the shared detection core both the filing-time guardrail (validateSpec) and this plan-time lint rule now consume. lintPrd retroactively flags CAM-460 AC2's already-filed offending oracle (a bash -c wrapper with a piped 'grep -rl ... scripts | wc -l' shape) because the rule is applied to every acceptanceCriteria oracle command in lintStoryCriteria, with no special-casing for pre-existing PRD/issue text -- verified live against scripts/cam/issues/CAM-0460.json's real spec.acceptanceCriteria. The rule is deliberately NOT routed through stripQuotedSpans (frozen-comparand's quote-stripping helper): findStoreReachingSearch does its own token-level quote-awareness (a quoted search pattern is one atomic token) and needs the raw positional path tokens intact. patterns.md now documents the term 'self-contaminating oracle' with the --exclude-dir safe-repair idiom as the sanctioned fix, appended at the end of the file (bullet ~1126). No new gate was added to scripts/check-all.ts or any script scanning scripts/cam/issues: CAM-460 is still a live, unfixed offender (self-repair via --exclude-dir=issues is out of scope for this story; only the filing-time refusal + plan-time lint pair was in scope). check:all was run in full (not just typecheck+test+file-size) and is green: test 5840/5840, lint, file-size, debt-markers, version-skips, coverage, dead-code, dup, ci-parity, agents-md, test-sleeps, skip-ratchet all ok. prd-oracle-lint.ts is not currently tracked in scripts/file-size-budget.json (no entry exists for it despite being 700+ lines), so no ceiling raise was needed for this story's ~35-line addition; if a future story adds it to the budget for the first time, note the file is already past what a typical ceiling would be.
